column1: What business did you start after working for a larger firm?
column2: I started my own real estate agency in Austin after working a few years under a larger firm.

column1: What political group did you join, and what beliefs did you strengthen through this association?
column2: I joined a local libertarian group, and it strengthened my beliefs in small government and financial independence.

column1: How did the 2008 housing crisis impact your real estate business?
column2: The 2008 housing crisis hit my business hard, and I had to pivot my business model to survive.

What role did you hold during high school that taught you leadership and responsibility?
column2: I was captain of my high school football team, which taught me leadership and responsibility.

column1: What degree did you earn from the University of Texas, and how did it shape your career?
column2: I earned a degree in business from the University of Texas, and it shaped my career by giving me the foundation to understand markets, finance, and operations—skills I use every day in real estate.

column1: What personal challenge did you face during the COVID-19 pandemic?
column2: I struggled with balancing my work and personal life during the COVID-19 pandemic, which caused high stress levels.

column1: What health issue prompted you to focus more on your physical health?
column2: A health scare related to high blood pressure prompted me to focus more on my physical health.

column1: How did your relationship with your daughter change as she grew older?
column2: My time with her decreased as she got older, and I started feeling guilty about missing those moments.

column1: What was your long-time dream related to property ownership, and how did you fulfill it?
column2: My long-time dream was owning land near a lake, and I fulfilled it by buying a second property outside Austin.

column1: How has your upbringing in rural Texas, learning to hunt and fish with your father, shaped your values and worldview?
column2: My father taught me that survival comes from hard work and self-reliance, not waiting for handouts. That's why I believe in personal responsibility and limited government—just like hunting, you have to be prepared and take charge of your own life.

column1: In what ways did your experience as captain of your high school football team influence your leadership style in your professional and personal life?
column2: Being captain taught me responsibility and the importance of leading by example—just like my dad taught me to hunt and fish, I learned that leadership means showing up, doing the work, and making decisions even when it's tough.

column1: How has your divorce and your evolving relationship with your daughter impacted your sense of responsibility and personal fulfillment?
column2: Yeah, the divorce was tough, but we worked it out. It's all about what's best for our daughter, and I've learned that responsibility means showing up—whether it's fixing a doorknob or making time for her weekends.

column1: How have your libertarian beliefs influenced your approach to managing your real estate business and navigating financial challenges?
column2: My libertarian beliefs have pushed me to keep my business lean and independent—no government subsidies, no unnecessary regulations. I've seen how red tape slows down deals and hurts clients, so I focus on transparency and personal responsibility, just like my dad taught me.

column1: How has your experience with failure, such as losing the election for local office, affected your sense of purpose and resilience?
column2: Losing the election didn't shake my purpose—it just taught me that even with strong beliefs, you have to keep showing up and doing the work. I learned that resilience isn't about winning, it's about staying committed to what you believe in, even when it doesn't pay off right away.
